| [CLAIM-454](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-454.md) v3 | A latent feature or mode recovered from an organization's members' activity is at most a constituent of an organizational perspective, not the perspective: a feature allocation says which members take part in which modes, and whether those modes are organized into one perspective depends on the relations of access, uptake and authority among their carriers, which the same allocation leaves open | From the Northstar turns of the exchange "Experimental Infrastructure Review", where the owner proposed inferring an organization's perspectives with hLDA (T21) and the Indian buffet process (T22). | [CLAIM-457](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-457.md) | That no single institution can bring about a remedy does not imply that no combination of them can: the institutions able together to realize a corrective outcome need include none able alone, so a true statement of unilateral inability is not a statement that the outcome is unattainable | A8 and A9 of the exchange of 2026-10-26, on the owner's CECOT case at U7: the United States said it could not bring a man back from Salvadoran custody, and El Salvador's president that he could not send him. | [CLAIM-490](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-490.md) | A fanbase is a mixture of spectators who relate to the club in different ways, as supporters, followers, fans and flâneurs, so the public stance credited to it is weighted towards the most committed types before any bias in who is sampled | From Giulianotti's taxonomy ([THEORY-1111](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1111.md)): supporters are hot and bound to the club as community, while flâneurs are cool consumers who switch clubs. | [CLAIM-526](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-526.md) v2 | Describing persons and organizations as coexisting levels of one process removes the question of how already-constituted agents add up to a collective, but not the question of levels: whether a collective variable has dynamics of its own, closed against the activity that realizes it, can be decided on a process description that presupposes no agents, is sometimes decided no, and a closed collective variable can be an aggregate that coexists with its realization while keeping none of its members' distinctions | Filed on reading Bencherki & Iliadis 2021 and Bencherki, Brummans & Vézy 2024, who hold that the "scaling up" problem "vanishes the moment communication is viewed eventfully" ([LIT-1902](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1902.md), p. 1364) because persons and organizations are "different informational levels that preserve all the characteristics of their organized components" ([LIT-1922](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1922.md), ms. p. 21, proposition 2). The record's closure results show what survives. What vanishes is the picture of agents adding up. What remains is whether a higher variable runs on its own, which is a question about variables and is decidable. The record's own case of a closed collective variable is a sum, an aggregate, that coexists with its units, so "stages or coexisting levels" is not a dichotomy. It does not say that the agent picture is right, or that organizations are aggregates of members. | Active |
| [CLAIM-529](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-529.md) v4 | An organization can be individuated without presupposing it as a declared candidate whose verdict can come out false: criteria stated on the candidate's interactions (whether benefit can be booked per member, which interactions the others depend on, what removing an interaction type does, whether its order survives release from an outside scaffold) apply to a grouping not yet assumed to be a unit, while criteria stated as members' attitudes toward the group (a goal about it, belonging, identity) make it partly constituted by being taken as one, individuating it by a different relation, unavailable where members have no such attitudes | Filed on re-reading Griesemer & Shavit 2023 ([LIT-188](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-188.md), [NOTE-173](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-173.md)). The body holds the parts of an answer, and they are of two kinds. | [CLAIM-531](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-531.md) v4 | Generative entrenchment does not by itself give organizational closure: an entrenched core, which later interactions depend on so that perturbing it is catastrophic and perturbing them tolerable, can sit at the root of an acyclic dependency order, and where interactions turn over such an order persists only while something outside supplies its core; an organization that is both entrenched and closed has a core containing a cycle of mutual maintenance, each interaction on which is itself core unless its share of the maintenance is redundant | Filed on re-reading Griesemer & Shavit 2023 ([LIT-188](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-188.md), [NOTE-173](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-173.md)), who mark the step from conexus to community by generative entrenchment of core interactions and then, with "Hence", by organizational closure. It does not say their communities lack closure, only that entrenchment and knockout do not show it; and it reads Wimsatt's concept only as they quote it. | Active |

Contributors who object without the capacity to change a decision can found a new organization in which their objection governs. | [CLAIM-615](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-615.md) v9 | An organized individual's identity over time is carried by the causal transmission of the relations that keep its repertoire realizable, not by its constituents or by any structure invariant across its realizations, so a structuralism about individuals has to be historical: the structure can change under maps that are not isomorphisms while the individual continues, two structurally identical copies can be two individuals, the transmitting organization may lie outside the individual, and when those relations part at a succession, different successors can continue different respects of it | The thesis of U14 to U17 of the exchange "Individuation, Possibility, and Disposition" (2026-11-06 to 07), from A32 §12 to A37's "synthesis in one statement", the version filed. | [CLAIM-678](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-678.md) v5 | Power over a technological arrangement has at least three dimensions that can be held and distributed separately: operational power, over how it works; economic power, over who owns it and takes its benefits; and epistemic power, over the knowledge needed to understand, evaluate and challenge it; so widening one, by public ownership, consumer choice or technical literacy, does not of itself widen the others | A's, from A11 §5 of the exchange "Analyze technological civilization trap" (2026-11-13), drawing on Mumford, Feenberg and Zuboff: "we should examine technological power in three dimensions", operational ("Who determines how the system works?"), economic ("Who owns the assets and captures the benefits?") and epistemic ("Who possesses the knowledge needed to understand, evaluate, and challenge it?"). | [CLAIM-690](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-690.md) v3 | Whichever way a whole and its part depend on each other, the same magnitude of dependence can run either way, and what sorts it is who controls the terms on which it is met, exit, renegotiation and the conditions of supply, while the magnitude and the integration that produced it set only how much rides on it: with the part able to withdraw or renegotiate, the whole's need of it becomes the part's hold on its terms; with the terms at an agent's discretion, the same need gives the part none, and the part's own dependence becomes vulnerability to that agent, on whom, under a principle grounding obligations in such vulnerability, the strengthened responsibility falls | The assistant's, offered at step 12 of the filing of "About Plantation Paradise" ([#488](https://github.com/dmarx/nucleation/issues/488)) and accepted by the owner on 2026-11-13. | [CLAIM-876](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-876.md) | The organization whose reproduction of occluding representations and allocations of authority breaches the second-order duty of answerability is a relational arrangement, the ground and object of the verdict and not its bearer; the duty falls on the agents or roles that control that reproduction, inside the arrangement or outside it, each as far as its control reaches, so that where no one controls it the duty is breached by no one | For [LEAD-131](../../../record/leads.d/LEAD-131.md), reading (a), an alternative to [CLAIM-877](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-877.md), and the assistant's lean. [CLAIM-624](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-624.md) says "an organization" breaches a duty of answerability, declares no sense of [TERM-074](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-074.md), and disclaims that the organization is an agent. | [CLAIM-910](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-910.md) | Where a shared external driver and members' coupling produce the same within-group correlation, features inferred from members' activity under a finite Indian buffet prior do not tell them apart and do not add to the communication graph in predicting interventions on the coupling; the graph alone invents coupling under the driver, and the features do not remove it | Found by [LEAD-144](../../../record/leads.d/LEAD-144.md)'s study ([CASE-337](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-337.md)), 2026-11-22. | [CLAIM-945](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-945.md) | Where members interact only through answers about stimuli a shared world supplies, a deviation in some members' interpretation reaches the others' interpretations only weakly, so a criterion of shared perspective that measures dependence by how far the others move finds no shared perspective even where members evaluate one another's answers against a common standard; the coupling shows in how fast the deviants are drawn back and in whether the others' response follows the standard | [LEAD-087](../../../record/leads.d/LEAD-087.md) stated a criterion of shared perspective in advance ([TERM-149](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-149.md)) and ran [CASE-145](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-145.md)'s populations through it ([CASE-362](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-362.md)). | [CLAIM-959](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-959.md) | Where membership in a whole is normatively thick, a collective institution that is an agent or a cooperative scheme its constituents belong to, constitution can ground an obligation the whole owes a constituent that it owes no outsider, under an independently justified principle of associative obligation, with the whole, where it can owe, as the bearer | The alternative reading to [CLAIM-960](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-960.md), for [LEAD-110](../../../record/leads.d/LEAD-110.md): [CASE-256](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-256.md)'s first result, read for a whole whose membership is normatively thick — a collective institution that is an agent ([TERM-074](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-074.md) sense 3), or a cooperative scheme its constituents belong to. | [CLAIM-960](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-960.md) | For a whole that is a bare relational arrangement, being a constituent adds no obligation beyond those grounded in the constituent's vulnerability, interests, rights and exposure to power: the part-whole relation locates where an obligation applies without grounding it, and because such an arrangement is not an agent the obligation falls on the agents or roles that maintain, control or benefit from it, not on the whole | The assistant's, for [LEAD-110](../../../record/leads.d/LEAD-110.md): [CASE-256](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-256.md) worked through to its second result for the ground and its third for the bearer, read for the default sense of "whole" ([TERM-074](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-074.md) sense 1, a bare relational arrangement that need not be an agent). | [CLAIM-986](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-986.md) v2 | In the transmission criterion of identity over time, an outside maintainer's organization is part of what is transmitted just insofar as it holds organization the repertoire depends on that the individual does not carry and that a competent unrelated replacement, working from the individual, would not supply; a garage holds none of a car's, so a change of garage continues the car whole, while an unrelated new maintainer can continue a project only in the respects its code carries | Reading (b) of how [CLAIM-615](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-615.md)'s open slot is filled, for [LEAD-163](../../../record/leads.d/LEAD-163.md).
